description:
What If Earth Became a Black Hole?

To turn Earth into a black hole you would have to crush it down to about 2 centimeters across, the size of a marble. And the Moon would keep orbiting it.

Follow for daily trips through the universe. 🚀

Images: NASA, ESA, ESO and Wikimedia Commons (free licenses, credited in the video file's notes)

segments.text: If Earth turned into a black hole, you could hold it in your hand.

segments.text: Any object can become a black hole, if you squeeze it small enough.

segments.headline: Squeeze it small

segments.text: For Earth, all six sextillion tonnes would have to fit into a ball about eighteen millimeters wide.
That's the size of a marble.
Here's the weird part: the Moon wouldn't fall in. It would keep orbiting, because Earth's mass, and its pull, would be the same.
segments.headline: The Moon keeps orbiting

segments.text: The Sun would need to shrink to about six kilometers across. Smaller than a city.

visual.label: the Sun as a black hole

segments.text: Luckily, neither of them is heavy enough to ever collapse like that on their own.
segments.headline: Don't panic

segments.text: Next stop: Time Dilation. Would you hold a marble-sized black hole? Just kidding. Don't. Tell me what you'd do in the comments, and follow for the next stop.
